supported_claims.claim_text: Turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek announced that Turkey's justice ministry requested the interior ministry to issue Interpol red notices for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and one other suspect.
The Turkish arrest warrants for Netanyahu and the other suspect were issued on July 14.
The charges in the Turkish warrants include genocide, crimes against humanity, and torture, stemming from Israel's interception of the Global Sumud Flotilla in May.
Erdogan's office responded to Israel's statement by condemning it as 'petty political tactics' and an attempt to portray Turkey as a threat.
France, Italy, and Australia have also launched judicial proceedings related to the interception of the flotilla.
Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir previously released a video of himself provoking detained flotilla activists who were bound on their knees.

Listen Listen (3 mins) Save Click here to share on social media share-nodes Share facebook x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu [File: Ronen Zvulun/Reuters] By Al Jazeera Staff and Reuters Published On 21 Aug 2026 21 Aug 2026 Turkiye has sought an international arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, accusing him of “genocide” for Israel’s attack in May on activists aboard the Global Sumud Flotilla for Gaza . In a post on X on Friday, Turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said arrest warrants had been issued on July 14 for Netanyahu and another suspect. Charges included genocide, crimes against humanity and torture, as part of a case against 35 people over the Israeli interception in international waters. Recommended Stories list of 4 items list 1 of 4 Turkiye unveils its first intercontinental ballistic missile: What we know list 2 of 4 Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan sign joint defence agreement: What’s in it? list 3 of 4 NATO summit begins: Who’s attending and what’s at stake? list 4 of 4 Turkiye says Mecca defence pact not aimed at Iran end of list “In line with the arrest warrants issued against Benjamin Netanyahu … our justice ministry has requested that ⁠the interior ministry issue [Interpol] red notices for them so that they may be sought ⁠internationally,” Gurlek said. Turkiye will use all available legal mechanisms to ensure Israel is held accountable for its crimes in Gaza, he added. NATO member Turkiye has been one of the fiercest critics of Israel’s genocidal war ⁠on Gaza and has previously issued domestic arrest warrants for Netanyahu over its attacks. Turkiye has also repeatedly called for international measures against Israel for what Ankara calls its violations of human rights and international law. Israel denies those charges. In May, Israeli forces fired on at least two vessels from the Global Sumud Flotilla sailing towards ‌Gaza. It was making a renewed attempt to deliver aid to the enclave after earlier missions were intercepted by the Israeli military in international waters. Israel’s interception of the flotilla provoked international outcry. France, Italy and Australia have also launched judicial proceedings. Advertisement About 50 vessels were in the Global Sumud Flotilla that left Turkiye in May heading for the besieged Palestinian territory. The activists were detained in the Mediterranean by the Israeli military and then taken to an Israeli prison before being deported . Israel’s far right National Security Minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir caused outrage at the time by releasing a video of himself angrily provoking flotilla activists who were on their knees with their hands tied behind their backs. “We will not allow the crimes committed in Gaza to be covered up or those responsible to be protected by a shield of impunity,” Gurlek said. “We will resolutely use all means available under national and international law.” Asked about Gurlek’s statement, Netanyahu’s office said: “[Turkish President] Erdogan’s pathetic attempt to intimidate ⁠the leaders and soldiers of Israel, the only true democracy in the ⁠Middle East, will go nowhere.” His office accused Erdogan of being “antisemitic” and vowed that Israel would “continue to act forcefully against Turkiye’s attempts to destabilise the region”. The useful fact is not simply that an approval exists; it is what the State Department’s record defines—and what it does not. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/).

## What the document establishes

The Bureau of Political-Military Affairs issued a congressional notification on August 21, 2026, identified as Transmittal #26-92. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). The record says the State Department approved a possible Foreign Military Sale to the Government of Italy for Guidance Section Single Variant Air-to-Air Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System-II and related equipment. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). It identifies Italy’s request as 5,031 Guidance Sections Single Variant Air-to-Air Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System-II WGU 59B/B. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). The document assigns the possible sale an estimated total cost of $364 million. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/).

## Why this record is useful

The notification links four elements in one official record: the approving department, the requesting government, the requested quantity and the estimated value. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). It also supplies a dated transmittal number that readers can use to distinguish this notification from any later official record concerning the same possible sale. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). That specificity makes the document a useful baseline for tracking whether the proposal changes or advances. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/).

## The procedural boundary

The document consistently describes the matter as a possible or proposed sale and presents itself as a congressional notification. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). Its approval language therefore does not, by itself, establish a concluded agreement, a contract award, a completed transaction, delivery or operational use. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). The $364 million figure should likewise be read as the estimated total cost attached to the possible sale, not as proof that this amount has been spent, received or booked. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/).

## What would establish the next phase

A later official record would need to confirm that the process advanced beyond the notification stage before readers could describe the transaction as completed or implemented. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). Such evidence could take the form of an official confirmation of a concluded agreement, a contract award, a delivery or another clearly identified implementation step. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). Until that evidence appears, the narrow conclusion remains that the State Department approved and notified Congress of a possible sale with a stated request and estimated value. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/).

omitted_unsupported_claims.claim_text: Benjamin Netanyahu's office dismissed the Turkish warrants as a 'pathetic attempt to intimidate' and accused Turkish President Erdogan of being antisemitic.
Turkey has just issued an arrest warrant for Israeli PM Netanyahu and is seeking an Interpol Red Notice, representing a severe and immediate escalation in Middle Eastern geopolitical tensions.

supported_claims.claim_text: Turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek announced that Turkey's justice ministry requested the interior ministry to issue Interpol red notices for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and one other suspect.
The Turkish arrest warrants for Netanyahu and the other suspect were issued on July 14.
The charges in the Turkish warrants include genocide, crimes against humanity, and torture, stemming from Israel's interception of the Global Sumud Flotilla in May.
Erdogan's office responded to Israel's statement by condemning it as 'petty political tactics' and an attempt to portray Turkey as a threat.
France, Italy, and Australia have also launched judicial proceedings related to the interception of the flotilla.
Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir previously released a video of himself provoking detained flotilla activists who were bound on their knees.

evidence_documents.canonical_content_text: Turkiye accuses Israel’s Netanyahu of ‘genocide’, seeks Interpol warrant | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera Skip links Skip to Content play Live Sign up Show navigation menu Navigation menu News Show more news sections Africa Asia US & Canada Latin America Europe Asia Pacific Middle East Explained Sport Opinion Video More Show more sections Features Economy Human Rights Climate Crisis Investigations Interactives In Pictures Science & Technology Podcasts Travel Sponsored Content play Live Click here to search search Sign up Navigation menu caret-left Israel-Palestine conflict Shackled, bleeding, raped: Abuse in Israeli prisons ‘This is an apartheid regime’ Does Trump have real leverage over Netanyahu? History of flotilla campaigns caret-right News | Israel-Palestine conflict Turkiye accuses Israel’s Netanyahu of ‘genocide’, seeks Interpol warrant Netanyahu and Erdogan trade insults as Ankara seeks warrant for Israel’s attacks on Global Sumud Flotilla activists headed for Gaza. Listen Listen (3 mins) Save Click here to share on social media share-nodes Share facebook x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu [File: Ronen Zvulun/Reuters] By Al Jazeera Staff and Reuters Published On 21 Aug 2026 21 Aug 2026 Turkiye has sought an international arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, accusing him of “genocide” for Israel’s attack in May on activists aboard the Global Sumud Flotilla for Gaza . In a post on X on Friday, Turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said arrest warrants had been issued on July 14 for Netanyahu and another suspect. Charges included genocide, crimes against humanity and torture, as part of a case against 35 people over the Israeli interception in international waters. Recommended Stories list of 4 items list 1 of 4 Turkiye unveils its first intercontinental ballistic missile: What we know list 2 of 4 Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan sign joint defence agreement: What’s in it? list 3 of 4 NATO summit begins: Who’s attending and what’s at stake? list 4 of 4 Turkiye says Mecca defence pact not aimed at Iran end of list “In line with the arrest warrants issued against Benjamin Netanyahu … our justice ministry has requested that ⁠the interior ministry issue [Interpol] red notices for them so that they may be sought ⁠internationally,” Gurlek said. Turkiye will use all available legal mechanisms to ensure Israel is held accountable for its crimes in Gaza, he added. NATO member Turkiye has been one of the fiercest critics of Israel’s genocidal war ⁠on Gaza and has previously issued domestic arrest warrants for Netanyahu over its attacks. Turkiye has also repeatedly called for international measures against Israel for what Ankara calls its violations of human rights and international law. Israel denies those charges. In May, Israeli forces fired on at least two vessels from the Global Sumud Flotilla sailing towards ‌Gaza. It was making a renewed attempt to deliver aid to the enclave after earlier missions were intercepted by the Israeli military in international waters. Israel’s interception of the flotilla provoked international outcry. France, Italy and Australia have also launched judicial proceedings. Advertisement About 50 vessels were in the Global Sumud Flotilla that left Turkiye in May heading for the besieged Palestinian territory. The activists were detained in the Mediterranean by the Israeli military and then taken to an Israeli prison before being deported . Israel’s far right National Security Minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir caused outrage at the time by releasing a video of himself angrily provoking flotilla activists who were on their knees with their hands tied behind their backs. “We will not allow the crimes committed in Gaza to be covered up or those responsible to be protected by a shield of impunity,” Gurlek said. “We will resolutely use all means available under national and international law.” Asked about Gurlek’s statement, Netanyahu’s office said: “[Turkish President] Erdogan’s pathetic attempt to intimidate ⁠the leaders and soldiers of Israel, the only true democracy in the ⁠Middle East, will go nowhere.” His office accused Erdogan of being “antisemitic” and vowed that Israel would “continue to act forcefully against Turkiye’s attempts to destabilise the region”. Soon after, in a post on X, Erdogan’s office denounced Netanyahu’s “petty political tactics” and condemned what it called the Israeli government’s attempt “to present Turkiye as a new threat”. aj-logo aj-logo aj-logo Advertisement About About Show more About Us Code of Ethics Terms and Conditions EU/EEA Regulatory Notice Privacy Policy Cookie Policy Cookie Preferences Accessibility Statement Sitemap Work for us Connect Connect Show more Contact Us User Accounts Help Advertise with us Stay Connected Newsletters Channel Finder TV Schedule Podcasts Submit a Tip Paid Partner Content Our Channels Our Channels Show more Al Jazeera Arabic Al Jazeera English Al Jazeera Investigative Unit Al Jazeera Mubasher Al Jazeera Documentary Al Jazeera Balkans AJ+ Our Network Our Network Show more Al Jazeera Centre for Studies Al Jazeera Media Institute Learn Arabic Al Jazeera Centre for Public Liberties & Human Rights Al Jazeera Forum Al Jazeera Hotel Partners Follow Al Jazeera English: facebook twitter youtube instagram-colored-outline rss © 2026 Al Jazeera Media Network

The useful fact is not simply that an approval exists; it is what the State Department’s record defines—and what it does not. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/).

## What the document establishes

The Bureau of Political-Military Affairs issued a congressional notification on August 21, 2026, identified as Transmittal #26-92. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). The record says the State Department approved a possible Foreign Military Sale to the Government of Italy for Guidance Section Single Variant Air-to-Air Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System-II and related equipment. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). It identifies Italy’s request as 5,031 Guidance Sections Single Variant Air-to-Air Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System-II WGU 59B/B. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). The document assigns the possible sale an estimated total cost of $364 million. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/).

## Why this record is useful

The notification links four elements in one official record: the approving department, the requesting government, the requested quantity and the estimated value. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). It also supplies a dated transmittal number that readers can use to distinguish this notification from any later official record concerning the same possible sale. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). That specificity makes the document a useful baseline for tracking whether the proposal changes or advances. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/).

## The procedural boundary

The document consistently describes the matter as a possible or proposed sale and presents itself as a congressional notification. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). Its approval language therefore does not, by itself, establish a concluded agreement, a contract award, a completed transaction, delivery or operational use. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). The $364 million figure should likewise be read as the estimated total cost attached to the possible sale, not as proof that this amount has been spent, received or booked. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/).

## What would establish the next phase

A later official record would need to confirm that the process advanced beyond the notification stage before readers could describe the transaction as completed or implemented. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). Such evidence could take the form of an official confirmation of a concluded agreement, a contract award, a delivery or another clearly identified implementation step. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/). Until that evidence appears, the narrow conclusion remains that the State Department approved and notified Congress of a possible sale with a stated request and estimated value. [United States Department of State](https://www.state.gov/releases/bureau-of-political-military-affairs/2026/08/italy-guidance-section-single-variant-air-to-air-advanced-precision-kill-weapon-system-ii/).
